headline: Rangers sign Luke Glendening to PTO
take:
Per Daily Faceoff, the Rangers have signed Luke Glendening to a professional tryout (PTO). Glendening failed to make the Tampa Bay Lightning roster out of training camp.

The deal is low risk, and the numbers suggest New York has a reasonable base to work from. The Rangers sit at 6-3-1 with 13 points through 10 games, and they hold 52.8 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season. That says they have slightly outplayed opponents, but the results lag behind: their goals scored are 4.3 below what their chances would predict. Their goalies have covered for it, saving 6.9 more goals than expected given the shots faced. At five-on-five the share drops to 51 percent, so the edge is thin.

For a depth signing, that context matters. Tampa Bay carries a 59 percent expected goals share at five-on-five and still let Glendening go, which says something about how crowded that roster is. New York's penalty kill allows 0.51 expected goals per game, a solid mark, so any role Glendening earns would need to fit a unit that is already working. Treat it as roster depth, not a needle mover.
